material_findings: GRASP applies an edit in about 64% of batches, rejects all four candidates in 36%, and admits about 16% of generated candidates overall; selective non-promotion is operationally substantial.
Probe size and candidate count are non-monotone controls: N=36 and K=4 outperform both smaller and larger surfaced settings, so proposal-to-evidence ratio matters.

The public GRASP mirror omits candidate/update logs and full rollouts, preventing independent reconstruction of exact acceptance chronology and late-round repeated-probe behavior from the released mirror alone.
MUSE-Autoskill supports unit-test-gated lifecycle engineering, but the gate's causal contribution and clean cross-task generalization are not isolated as sharply as GRASP.
